title: Events-pass coverage audit (task #40) + BEAM event_ordering autopsy
method: LLM audit, no GPU: three Claude Sonnet 5 auditors each read 10 rows' haystack sessions from evals/data/longmemeval_oracle.json and enumerated the gold supporting evidence with verbatim quotes; a fourth read all 23 served BEAM event_ordering rows (hybrid_ev_response != hybrid_response as the served proxy). The orchestrating session verified every packet's output ids and spot/full-verified quotes against the sessions (packet 2: 20/20 quotes exact; packets 1/3: 3-row spot checks, all exact), then joined auditor labels with cue/serving ground truth from the committed aggserve-0806 rows: a null served block counts as cue-miss ONLY when has_aggregation_cue and has_temporal_cue are both false on the question; with a cue fired it is an extraction-or-retrieval gap. Scope: the 24 multi-session residual rows (rag right, hybrid_ev_syn wrong) plus the 6 syn-win rows as contrast, from evals/results/longmemeval-all-oracle-qwen-27b-aggserve-0806.jsonl.
headline_findings: 19 of 24 residual rows are amount-arithmetic: they need numeric values combined across sessions, not more bare occurrences. 19/24 need the event to CARRY a quantity.

The quantity is being stripped at extraction: e.g. a346bb18's session says 'completed my first full marathon in 4h 22min' and the served event reads 'completed first full marathon'; cc06de0d's 'took a taxi, which cost me $12' served without the $12. The chronicle schema needs NO change - description is free text; the v1 events prompt simply never asks for quantities.

The win rows prove the mechanism end-to-end: 3fdac837's events carried '4-day trip' and 'from April 15th to 22nd' in their descriptions and the answerer computed the total correctly. Quantity in description = win; quantity dropped = loss, on otherwise-matching row shapes.
5 residual rows never fired a cue at all: 'total amount', 'total distance', 'the most money', 'average' are outside the has_aggregation_cue regex. One-line service fix.
7 rows are not-event-shaped (static facts: siblings, GPA, leadership percentage, premise-verification) - events cannot help these; they bound the ceiling of any events-side fix at ~15/24.

Win-attribution caveat: by served_match >= half of gold evidence, 4 of 6 syn wins are attributable to the served events; the packet-3 auditor's stricter reading attributes only 2 of 6 (3fdac837, 60159905) fully, meaning some wins rode on non-events context. The paired deltas remain valid either way; only the mechanism story for individual wins softens.

findings: Zero of 23 rows are 'wrong-order-despite-events': no case exists where the model had the right occurrences and merely sequenced them wrong. Where the block contained the queried items (20/1), the model ordered them correctly BY ITSELF (0.0 -> 0.8) with no synthesis scaffold.

6 of 8 regressions are abstention-suppression: hybrid had answered from ordinary retrieval (e.g. 16/1 scored 0.5; 13/0 scored 0.6) and hybrid_ev collapsed to 'I don't know' (0.0) - the model treats a served-but-partial events block as authoritative and exhaustive and stops using the rest of the context. Same family as the TiMem window-gate claim-suppression ('key gravity') lesson.
The remaining 2 regressions are distraction (real but rubric-irrelevant events crowding out facts hybrid had).
beam_event_ordering_autopsy.verdict: Answer-time ordering synthesis is evidence-dead as an experiment: it would have prevented zero of the eight regressions. The evidence-backed interventions are (a) coverage - the same fix the LME audit demands - and (b) an anti-suppression serving header marking the block as a partial record so the model keeps using the surrounding context.
beam_event_ordering_autopsy.artifact_note: Per-row classifications with quoted evidence are in the orchestration transcript; counts above derive from the 23 committed rows in evals/results/beam-100K-qwen-27b-beam100k-ev-0806.jsonl and are recomputable from responses alone (served proxy + score deltas).

recommended_next: events_pass_v2 prompt: KEEP QUANTITIES verbatim in the description + exhaustiveness mandate (every distinct occurrence). No schema change. Ships only through a measured gate (GPU, HELD).
has_aggregation_cue extension: total amount/distance/average/the most/spend-class phrasings. Service-side one-liner + tests.
Serving header: mark the events block as a partial record (anti-suppression). Bench variant arm first, production copy on a pass.
NOT recommended: answer-time ordering synthesis (see BEAM autopsy verdict).

rows.rationale: Three distinct luxury-purchase instances (evening gown, boots, handbag) are stated across the three sessions, each with an explicit dollar amount, and they sum exactly to the gold answer. served_events_block is null, so none of the three purchase instances reached the answer context at all; there is no evidence to tell whether they were never extracted as events or extracted but not retrieved, but either way nothing was served.

Four distinct cuisine-trying/learning instances are stated, one per session (Ethiopian, Indian, Vegan, Korean), matching the gold count of 4. Only the Ethiopian restaurant instance made it into served_events_block; the Indian cooking-class, vegan cooking-class, and Korean bibimbap instances were never served, so the answering model (syn) could only credit 3 cuisines total (it apparently recovered Indian and vegan from elsewhere in context but missed Korean, landing on 3).

Four grocery-spend instances (Trader Joe's $80, Walmart $120, Thrive Market $150, Publix $60+$10) are stated across the four sessions; comparing them picks out Thrive Market as gold. served_events_block is null, so none of the four spend instances were available to the answering model, which instead surfaced an unrelated Walmart mention with the wrong amount ($120 vs. the actual $120 stated, but not the maximum).

Only two completed (past-tense) doctor visits fall in March: Dr. Smith on March 3 and Dr. Thompson on March 20 (the EMG with Dr. Johnson is scheduled for April 1, i.e. future and out of window, and the gastroenterologist appointment is only 'considering scheduling'). served_events_block actually contains both: a dated entry for the March 20 Thompson visit and an undated entry ('had an appointment with primary care physician') that corresponds to the Smith visit. Since both needed facts were served, syn's undercount to 1 looks like the model discounting the undated entry rather than a serving gap -- the missing date on that entry is a plausible proximate cause, but the instance itself was present.

Three market-sale instances are stated, each with an explicit dollar figure (one requiring a unit-price x quantity multiplication), summing exactly to $495. served_events_block is null, so none reached the answer context; syn recovered only two of the three sales from elsewhere (totaling $345) and missed the $7.50 x 20 potted-plant sale entirely.

The user states an aggregate completed-course count on each of two platforms (3 on Coursera, 2 on edX) in two separate sessions; summing them gives the gold answer of 5. served_events_block is null, so neither platform-count statement reached the answer context, and syn only surfaced the edX figure (2), missing the Coursera figure (3) entirely.

This is the abstention (_abs) variant: the sessions establish a 20-gallon community tank (16 fish) and a separate 10-gallon betta tank, but never a 30-gallon tank, so the correct behavior is to decline. This is a premise-verification/fact-lookup task, not something an event chronicle (which tracks activities, not tank specs) could help with; syn instead hallucinated compliance, reporting 16 fish as if the 30-gallon premise were valid.

Two hikes on consecutive weekends are stated, each with an explicit mileage, summing to the gold 8 miles. served_events_block is null, so neither hike instance reached the answer context, and syn answered 'I don't know' outright.

The current-page statement and the total-page-count statement are made in two different sessions three days apart; subtracting gives the gold 190 pages remaining. served_events_block is null, so neither reading-progress instance reached the answer context, and syn answered 'I don't know'.

The $6 train fare and $12 taxi fare are each stated once, in different sessions; the gold answer is their $6 difference. served_events_block does include an entry for 'missed train and took a taxi' (matching the taxi instance) but strips out the $12 figure, and has no entry at all for the train-fare statement; a second served entry (signing up for the ride-sharing program) is irrelevant. Because neither served item carries a dollar amount, syn had nothing to compute from and answered 'I don't know' even though one of the two underlying events was represented.

Both statements are genuine personal actions (packing luggage, wearing footwear on the trip) that a well-tuned extractor should surface as events, but served_events_block is null, so no cue fired at all for this question even though event-shaped material existed in both sessions.

The purchase itself WAS captured as an event ('bought a book from a bookstore during a sale'), proving extraction and retrieval both worked here, but neither the $30 original price nor the $24 paid price -- stated in separate incidental asides -- was carried into the event text, so the served block is topically right but numerically empty.

Both statements are self-reported listening-progress counts embedded as asides in unrelated podcast-recommendation chat, and served_events_block is null, so nothing fired even though 'finished episode N' reads as a completion event; these are borderline event/state, but no evidence of extraction succeeding anywhere else in the packet suggests the cue simply never triggered.

The session-0 purchase event was served intact with its quantity ('purchased 5 coffee mugs ... for coworkers'), proving the pipeline can carry embedded counts; but the session-1 aside restating the same gift with its $60 total cost was never captured as its own instance, so the arm had the divisor but not the dividend.

served_events_block is null, yet syn_response independently states '1,800 miles... three recent road trips', meaning the model had partial non-event context on the second statement but never saw the 1,200-mile Yellowstone trip at all, confirming the events cue specifically missed both trip-distance mentions while some other channel leaked a fragment.

The purchase event was served ('purchased Jimmy Choo heels ... at the outlet mall') but stripped of the $200 price paid in the very same turn, and the $500 retail figure is a general market-price fact the user recalled (no personal action at all), so even perfect extraction of the purchase event would not have supplied both numbers needed.

Both statements are organizational headcount facts with no verb of personal occurrence -- nobody 'did' anything -- so this is a facts/values need rather than something an event log would ever naturally capture, independent of whether extraction or retrieval were tuned better.

The served block contains one real but irrelevant event ('booked a hotel in Tokyo'), proving the pipeline did extract and cue something for these sessions -- it just wasn't these quoted transportation prices, which are hearsay/quote facts rather than actions the user performed and so aren't naturally event-shaped.

View counts are live state metrics attached to a video ('has X views' as of the conversation), not a discrete occurrence at a point in time, so they sit outside what an event log is built to represent even though served_events_block being null also means no cue fired regardless.

GPA values are static personal-history attributes (like a profile field), not occurrences a user performed at a point in time, so this need is squarely facts/values rather than events -- no amount of event-extraction tuning would have produced a usable instance here.

The served event ('completed first full marathon') recorded that the race happened but stripped out both numbers the arithmetic needs -- neither the 4h22min finish time nor the 4h10min target appears anywhere in the block. An event that only asserts occurrence, with no attached duration, cannot answer a subtraction question no matter how well it was extracted.

Having siblings is a static biographical fact, not something that happened at a point in time -- there is no occurrence for an event extractor to notice, so served_events_block is null by construction. This is a state fact masquerading as a count, exactly the case the taxonomy singles out.

Both facts are recurring routine/schedule statements ('on Fridays I wake at X', 'on weekdays I wake at Y'), not discrete dated occurrences -- there is nothing event-shaped to extract here, which is consistent with the block being null.

served_events_block is null, correctly reflecting that no qualifying 'poster for undergrad project' event exists. The syn model still answered 'Harvard University' by splicing the thesis-research poster from one session with the Harvard conference mention from another, unrelated session -- a hallucination fabricated despite (not because of) the event pipeline, since nothing was served to it at all.

The served events enumerated 4 of the 5 kit instances as clean dated/undated bullets (F-15, Tiger I diorama, B-29 + Camaro purchase), which is exactly the representation instance-counting needs. The 5th kit (Spitfire Mk.V) is absent from the events block entirely, so this win is only partially attributable to the event chronicle -- the model must have recovered the Spitfire mention from context outside the shown events.

Both events preserved the actual duration cue in their text ('4-day trip', and the explicit date range 'April 15th to 22nd'), so both numbers needed for the sum were directly present in the served block without requiring further inference -- a clean case of the chronicle carrying quantities correctly.

Neither served event ('booked a trip with Sakura Travel Agency', 'paid by bank transfer') carries a dollar figure at all -- both quotes needed for the subtraction are absent from the block. On the evidence shown, this win cannot actually be attributed to the event chronicle; the model must have sourced the $2,500/$2,800 figures from some other context (e.g. a facts store) not reflected in served_events_block.

The events block captured only the current run's quantity ('finished a 5K run in 35 minutes'); the prior year's 45-minute time is absent. Only half the arithmetic input came from the event chronicle, yet the model produced the correct 10-minute delta, implying the other value reached it through some other channel.

All three dinner parties were extracted as discrete, correctly dated events, which is exactly the representation instance-counting needs -- a clean win for the event chronicle. RAG undercounted at two, apparently missing the Mike's BBQ mention buried mid-turn.

The single served event ('booked a hotel in Tokyo') is irrelevant to either transportation cost. Despite having nothing useful served, the model correctly recognized that the bus fare was never actually stated by the user (only speculated by the assistant) and abstained, unlike RAG which borrowed the assistant's suggested range as if it were a fact.
